function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how you can create a Compute Engine instance on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) that is equipped with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. > ⚠️ **Important note** – As of the latest GCP release, the RTX A6000 is *not* one of the officially supported GPU models in Compute Engine. > The closest available GPU families are the **NVIDIA Tesla A100** and **NVIDIA Tesla V100**. > If you truly need an RTX A6000, you would have to use a custom‑hardware solution or a different provider that offers that GPU. > The example below uses the **Tesla A100** (the next‑best GPU for most workloads) but you can replace it with any other supported GPU family if you wish. --- ## 1. Prerequisites | Item | How to set it up | |------|------------------| | **Project ID** | Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` with your actual GCP project ID. | | **Zone** | Replace `us-central1-a` with the zone where you want the instance. | | **Service Account** | Create a service account with the following IAM roles:
`roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`, `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`, `roles/compute.networkAdmin`. Download its JSON key. | | **gcloud SDK** | Install the [Google Cloud SDK](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install) and run `gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=path/to/key.json`. | --- ## 2. Using the `gcloud` CLI ```bash # Variables PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID" ZONE="us-central1-a" INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo" MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a100" # Replace with "nvidia-tesla-v100" if you prefer GPU_COUNT="1" IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts" IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud" # Create the instance gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \ --project="$PROJECT" \ --zone="$ZONE" \ --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \ --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \ --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \ --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \ --boot-disk-size=200GB \ --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \ --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \ --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \ --tags=http-server,https-server ``` ### What the command does | Flag | Purpose | |------|---------| | `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM configuration. | | `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. | | `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Installs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. | | `--boot-disk-size` | Gives the VM a 200 GB SSD boot disk. | | `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: runs a shell script at first boot (e.g., installs NVIDIA drivers). | | `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU driver installation). | | `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules. | --- ## 3. Using the REST API (JSON) If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), here’s the exact JSON payload you would POST to: ```json { "name": "rtx-a6000-demo", "machineType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8", "disks": [ { "boot": true, "autoDelete": true, "initializeParams": { "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts", "diskSizeGb": 200, "diskType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd" } } ], "networkInterfaces": [ { "network": "global/networks/default", "accessConfigs": [ { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" } ] } ], "serviceAccounts": [ { "email": "YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com", "scopes": [ "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" ] } ], "guestAccelerators": [ { "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100", "acceleratorCount": 1 } ], "metadata": { "items": [ { "key": "startup-script", "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470\n" } ] }, "tags": { "items": ["http-server", "https-server"] } } ``` ### How to call it ```bash curl -X POST \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d @instance.json \ "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances" ``` Replace `instance.json` with the path to the JSON file containing the payload above. --- ## 4. Startup Script (Optional) If you want the instance to automatically install the NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit on boot, create a file called `startup.sh` with the following content: ```bash #!/bin/bash # Update package lists apt-get update # Install NVIDIA driver (replace 470 with the latest supported version) apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470 # Install CUDA Toolkit (optional) apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-4 # Reboot to apply driver changes reboot ``` Make sure the script is executable (`chmod +x startup.sh`) and reference it in the `gcloud` command or the REST payload as shown above. --- ## 5. Verify the Instance After creation, you can verify that the GPU is attached and the driver is installed: ```bash # SSH into the instance gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-demo --zone=us-central1-a # Check GPU presence nvidia-smi ``` You should see the NVIDIA A100 (or your chosen GPU) listed with its driver version. --- ## 6. Clean Up When you’re done, delete the instance to avoid incurring charges: ```bash gcloud compute instances delete rtx-a6000-demo --zone=us-central1-a ``` --- ### TL;DR - **Command**: `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 ...` - **REST**: POST to `/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` with JSON payload including `"guestAccelerators"` section. - **Note**: RTX A6000 is not currently supported; use Tesla A100/V100 instead. Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or GPU count to match your workload requirements. Happy computing!
